sources.title: Replit: The Project Editor
sources.finding: The hosted Project Editor provides Agent chat, project tools, live preview and a task board in the browser.

sources.title: Replit: Mobile features; Navigate your project
sources.finding: Native iOS and Android clients support Agent, Tools and Tasks panes, project continuation and completion or help notifications.

sources.title: Replit: Agent modes
sources.finding: Replit Agent has Free, Power and Max modes; Auto routes paid work to models. Model routing does not establish support for a third-party coding harness.

sources.title: Replit: Agent billing
sources.finding: Replit plan credits pay for Agent and other cloud services; paid actions use effort-based pricing after confirmation.

sources.title: Replit: Getting started; Import code and design
sources.locator: Getting started; Import code and design
sources.finding: Start a project by describing an idea in plain language, or bring it in from GitHub, Figma or uploaded files, in the cloud Project Editor. The page names no templates and does not itself state that no local environment is needed.

sources.title: Replit: How background tasks work
sources.finding: A main-thread prompt can create titled tasks with descriptions and plans, or users can start a planning thread.

sources.title: Replit: Plan your tasks; Review and accept
sources.locator: Plan your tasks; Review and accept
sources.finding: Agent proposes detailed plans and definitions of done; users inspect View plan, accept tasks or request a revised plan before execution.

sources.title: Replit: Create and approve remaining tasks; Let Agent schedule the work
sources.locator: Create and approve remaining tasks; Let Agent schedule the work
sources.finding: Agent identifies prerequisite tasks and queues dependent work until the prerequisite is applied. The board shows the blocker.

sources.title: Replit: Your app is safe while tasks run
sources.locator: Your app is safe while tasks run
sources.finding: Each background task inherits the project context and receives its own Agent and project copy.

sources.title: Replit: Import code and design
sources.finding: Projects can begin from GitHub, Figma or uploaded files; this establishes input channels, not verified architecture comprehension.

sources.title: Replit: What is the task system; Frequently asked questions
sources.locator: What is the task system; Frequently asked questions
sources.finding: Native tasks have Drafts, Active, Ready and Done states, a board, separate threads and explicit acceptance. Draft planning sessions can be archived and restored; cancelling building work discards it.

sources.title: Replit: What is the task system
sources.finding: Agent can split a request into tasks and put them on the human-visible task board.

sources.title: Replit: Tasks start running; Availability
sources.finding: Core supports one active background task, Pro up to ten and Enterprise up to sixty-four. Additional tasks queue.

sources.title: Replit: Let Agent schedule the work
sources.finding: Agent schedules independent tasks when capacity exists and holds dependent tasks until prerequisites are applied.

sources.title: Replit: What is the task system; Review and apply
sources.locator: What is the task system; Review and apply
sources.finding: Replit Agent decomposes a request into background Agent tasks with separate threads and returns work logs, tests and previews to the main-version review flow.

sources.title: Replit: How Routines run; Availability and limits
sources.locator: How Routines run; Availability and limits
sources.finding: Paid-plan chat Routines repeat hourly, daily or weekly without a new request. They run in Power or Max, queue behind other chat work and do not schedule publishing.

sources.title: Replit: Frequently asked questions
sources.finding: Cancel stops building and discards its work. The main thread and each task thread permit follow-up direction.

sources.title: Replit: Board view
sources.finding: A project board displays Drafts, Active, Ready and Done tasks alongside task conversations. Fleet-scale navigation has not been tested.

sources.title: Replit: Plan mode; What you can build
sources.locator: Plan mode; What you can build
sources.finding: Users start with ordinary chat, refine plans and let Agent create task lists before approving work.

sources.title: Replit: Frequently asked questions
sources.finding: The cloud Project Editor saves files, history and the running app when the browser closes. This documents cloud persistence, not an unlimited Agent process lifetime.

sources.title: Replit: Tasks start running
sources.finding: Background tasks run in isolated project copies and do not change the main version until applied. The docs do not name these copies as containers, VMs or worktrees.

sources.title: Replit: What happens when I close my browser?
sources.locator: What happens when I close my browser?
sources.finding: Files, history and running app are preserved in the cloud for a later visit. No worker-crash recovery test was performed.

sources.title: Replit: What is Replit Agent?
sources.finding: Agent sets up the project and infrastructure. Specific dependency-cache, port-collision and clean-remote-host behavior remains untested.

sources.title: Replit: Control spending
sources.finding: Core and Pro Routines have per-run budgets checked after each step; an in-progress step can complete beyond the budget. Enterprise lacks the per-run budget.

sources.title: Replit: Review and apply
sources.finding: Finished tasks expose a work log, test results and preview; active threads and board cards show task status.

sources.title: Replit: Viewing Agent usage
sources.finding: Agent billing is effort-based and uses plan credits shared with cloud services. A controlled reconciliation against provider billing was not performed.

sources.title: Replit: Tasks start running
sources.finding: Plan-based task limits cause additional background tasks to queue until slots are available. This is not evidence of per-host CPU or RAM scheduling.

sources.title: Replit: Personal vs. team workspaces
sources.finding: Team workspaces share projects with members; Core includes five collaboration seats and Pro fifteen. Simultaneous co-prompt ordering is not established by this source.

sources.title: Replit: Personal vs. team workspaces; Managing members
sources.locator: Personal vs. team workspaces; Managing members
sources.finding: Personal workspaces have an admin and project guests; team workspaces add members with access to all workspace projects. Admins can invite and remove members.

sources.title: Replit: Configure single sign-on
sources.finding: SAML SSO requires Enterprise and organization/identity-provider admin access. SSO does not automatically invite users; invitations or SCIM manage membership.

sources.title: Replit: Review and accept; Review and apply
sources.locator: Review and accept; Review and apply
sources.finding: Humans approve plans before background execution and apply or dismiss finished changes before they affect the main version.

sources.title: Replit: Review and apply
sources.finding: Ready tasks expose a work log, test results and live preview with Apply or Dismiss decisions. Review effort and missed evidence were not measured.

sources.title: Replit: Review and apply
sources.finding: Task review retains a work log, test results and a live preview in the task flow. A cross-task artifact gallery was not established.

sources.title: Replit: App Testing
sources.finding: With App Testing enabled, Agent periodically tests apps it builds in an actual browser and fixes issues it finds; it is available for Full Stack JavaScript and Streamlit Python web apps. Documentation is not proof of mandatory independent review or an enforced passing test gate.

sources.title: Replit: Apply changes safely
sources.finding: Applying tasks invokes AI-assisted conflict resolution. The source does not establish a GitHub PR workflow.

sources.title: Replit: How do I publish my app?
sources.locator: How do I publish my app?
sources.finding: Users publish to a live URL from the Project Editor. Production authorization and revision binding were not tested.

sources.title: Replit: What happens if Agent makes a mistake?
sources.locator: What happens if Agent makes a mistake?
sources.finding: Agent creates checkpoints that users can roll back to when a change is wrong.

sources.title: Replit: Import code and design
sources.finding: Users can import GitHub projects and uploaded files. Exported task history and complete self-hosting are not established.

sources.title: Replit: Model improvement
sources.finding: Pro users can opt out of Model Improvement in Personalization settings; Replit states it does not use Enterprise customer content to train models. The page names no such control for Starter or Core.

sources.title: Replit: How billing works
sources.finding: Monthly plan credits cover Agent and other cloud services such as published apps, storage and databases under usage-based billing, with alerts, budget limits and purchasable credit packs. The page does not list network transfer or state an overage rate.

sources.title: Replit: Get support directly from Agent
sources.finding: The November 6 changelog documents Agent-assisted support investigation and Pro ticket submission. This is shipped release activity, not a shutdown notice.

sources.title: Replit: What you get; Limitations
sources.finding: Starter offers recurring daily Agent credits capped monthly and monthly cloud credits, with one published app whose public link expires after thirty days. Full build, connectors and Plan mode require Core.

sources.title: Replit: Effort-based pricing
sources.finding: Agent uses effort-based paid pricing with plan credits; actual charges depend on request complexity and cloud services. A fixed average task price is not documented.

sources.title: Replit: Starter Plan
sources.finding: Upgrading to Core gives more storage and monthly credits that also let users pay as they go.
